scope: Local source, unit, tenant/static migration, fresh and populated PostgreSQL 17.10, restricted-role, in-flight writer, current provider/CSV, privacy, replay, CLI-redaction/success, production-build, secret-scan, and dependency evidence for the opt-in one-way source-classification writer fence. No customer data, provider credential/request, source-system write, real prior deployable image, hosted database, representative volume, protected staging, production deployment, legal decision, compliance, or production-readiness claim is included.

priorEvidence.relationship: Extends the prior bounded repair evidence with migration 0052, a transaction-serialized activation boundary, deferred exact-classification enforcement, a one-way operating contract, and final 53-migration verification. It supersedes only that artifact's bounded old-writer race and mixed-writer control gap.

verificationCorrections.problemObserved: The initial cross-tenant activation scan relied on existing repair-owner RLS policies that did not explicitly authorize a plain source-event SELECT for activation.
verificationCorrections.correction: Add a migration-owner SELECT policy requiring both security-definer current_user and the dedicated maintenance session_user, then reject every non-maintenance session inside the activation function.
verificationCorrections.postCorrectionResult: Existing and in-flight gaps block activation; app, worker, maintenance-table, and direct migrator-session negative tests pass.

verificationCorrections.problemObserved: The first provider replay assertion expected only one publisher call, while the service deliberately republishes the same already-durable envelope after a duplicate receipt.
verificationCorrections.correction: Assert two equal dispatch envelopes while independently proving a single source classification and a total of only two durable outbox authorities across the provider and CSV writers.
verificationCorrections.postCorrectionResult: Duplicate dispatch semantics and durable idempotency are both represented accurately.

verificationCorrections.problemObserved: A combined selected run of the database suite followed by the existing repair suite found three deliberate unclassified test rows left by the first suite.
verificationCorrections.correction: Run each existing stateful integration suite against a fresh, exact named local test database; keep the new writer-fence suite fully isolated with create/drop lifecycle.
verificationCorrections.postCorrectionResult: The current 37-test database suite, two-test repair suite, and isolated one-test fence suite all pass from their documented clean boundaries.

repositoryState.oldWriterEvidenceType: synthetic database-effect transaction using the current schema and a classification-unaware insert

limitations: The repository has no commit and therefore no real prior deployable image; the old-writer test is a synthetic database-effect transaction, not a mixed-binary deployment rehearsal.
No representative source-event volume, activation scan duration, steady-state advisory-lock latency, WAL, disk, replica lag, or hosted PostgreSQL behavior was measured.
No protected staging, multi-host, supervisor restart, rollback-image, backup/PITR restore, failover, alert delivery, or production activation was exercised.
No authorized Shopify or Stripe sandbox request was made; current writer compatibility uses synthetic authenticated payloads and actual repository/service paths.

The fence protects source-event/classification atomicity and does not prove provider completeness, normalization correctness, reconciliation accuracy, financial savings, compliance, reliability, or production readiness.
Activation is one-way. Once enabled, an old classification-unaware writer is intentionally unavailable; rollback must use a compatible image or a separately reviewed future forward migration.
